stories.title: Pair held in Iran seen by UK officials after 112 days
stories.summary: BBC reports that Lindsay and Craig Foreman, a British couple held in Iran and sentenced to 10 years on espionage charges they deny, were visited at Evin Prison by UK officials for the first time in 112 days, according to their family. The FCDO was contacted for comment; this is BBC reporting, not an FCDO announcement.

stories.title: Half the harvest, twice the bills: how drought hit farms
stories.summary: BBC reports that drought sharply reduced West Country farm output: one Gloucestershire farm lost half its wheat harvest, dairy farmers used winter silage early as grass failed, and one Wiltshire farm put extra feed costs above £100,000.

stories.title: 'Unknown' Sheffield soldier named in Netherlands Ceremony
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence says investigators identified an unnamed Jonkerbos War Cemetery grave in the Netherlands as Sheffield-born Lance Corporal Ronald Smirthwaite, killed in 1945. A rededication service was organised after the identification.

stories.title: Grave of Cornish soldier missing since 1945 identified in Germany
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence's War Detectives identified the previously unnamed grave of Private Sidney Allen, a Cornwall-born Hampshire Regiment soldier killed in 1945, at Reichswald Forest War Cemetery. A rededication was held 81 years after his death.

stories.title: New duty proposed on imports of Chinese rutile titanium dioxide
stories.summary: The Trade Remedies Authority's initial recommendation proposes an anti-dumping measure on Chinese rutile titanium dioxide imports after finding dumping and an imminent threat of injury to UK production. This is a recommendation, not an enacted duty.

stories.title: Construction building materials: commentary September 2026
stories.summary: The official statistics report says August 2026 brick deliveries fell 10.1% year on year and block deliveries fell 6.5%, while the 'All Work' construction-materials price index rose 6.4% year on year.
stories.source: GOV.UK — Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

stories.title: Royal Mail plans to cut 2,500 jobs
stories.summary: Royal Mail announced plans to remove 2,500 head-office and support roles by the end of 2027, about 2% of its 131,000 workforce. The proposed reduction would be through voluntary redundancies and people leaving; frontline posties and drivers are excluded and unions are in formal consultation.
